description: Find businesses AI agents can reach, by a few words in any language (query: "florist", "hotel em Lisboa"), a place (near: a town or a point; country), category (list_categories), language, open_now, attributes and payments (list_attributes), price_band, and what their doors take (accepts, requestable, door_type, level, has_inbox). Every filter only leaves businesses out; from rules version 12, a search with no match for every word near a place is run again with its kind's words, and an answer to a search for more than its place with nobody near it names in note the nearest that match. Results come by how well they match, then in the published order, which nobody can pay to change; each lists the business's own doors. Only agent-ready businesses are listed; software, API and AI companies only when asked for (category software-ai). This server books and sells nothing: talk to the business at its doors. Pages of up to 20: pass next_cursor as cursor.

accepts.description: What its live doors take and what it accepts as payment, all of them: ask, quote, book, order, pay, or a payment from list_attributes like card or pix. This only leaves businesses out.

attributes.description: Keys from list_attributes, like "delivery" or "walk_ins", or key=value for one with values; every one must hold. This only leaves businesses out.

category.description: A slug from list_categories (hair-beauty) or a place category id (hair_salon), with every category below it; its label or a synonym works too. Anything else is an error naming categories to try.

country.description: A country code like PT or BR: a business located there, serving it or shipping there. This only leaves businesses out.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous answer, for the next page of the same search.

door_type.description: A live door of any of these types: inbox, mcp, a2a, openapi, api, ucp, acp, nlweb, other, "platform" for any platform, or platform:<name>. This only leaves businesses out.

has_inbox.description: true: with an inbox door; false: without one. This only leaves businesses out.

item_type.description: Only businesses whose inbox takes this; stay: a place to stay whose inbox takes stays.

language.description: Only businesses that speak this language, as a tag like pt or en; pt also finds pt-br.

level.description: At this readiness level or above: askable (an AI can ask), bookable or orderable (a door takes bookings or orders: one rung), payable. Nothing below askable is listed.

limit.description: How many to return: 10 when left out.

radius_km.description: How far from the point, in kilometres: 10 when left out.

place.description: A town's name, like Lisboa or New York.

radius_km.description: How far from the town's centre, in kilometres: more for a larger town when left out.

near.description: Only businesses within radius_km of a place, each with its distance: a town's name ("Lisboa"), {place, radius_km}, or a point {lat, lng, radius_km}. Most businesses sell online and have no location yet: the answer says when none is there.

open_now.description: true: only businesses open right now by the hours they published. One that published no hours is left out.

order.description: rank: the published order (the default); nearest: by distance, then the published order, however well each matches query, and it needs near.

price_band.description: 1 (cheapest) to 4, as "2" or a range "1-2". This only leaves businesses out.

q.description: Another name for query (the REST API's); given both, query is the one searched.

query.description: A few words about what the business does or where, in any language: "florist", "bike repair", "hotel em Lisboa". Every word must match a whole word of its name, categories, services, tags, description or town (itself, its plural or its singular), or, for a word of four letters or more as written, the beginning of one ("bake" finds bakery), ignoring capitals and accents; in a script written without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai), anywhere inside a text; a word naming a category matches its businesses. Unless near is given, a town after "in" or "near" becomes near, and a country after "in" becomes country. "open" belongs in open_now. A search for what a door does ("book a hotel in Lisbon", "order pizza", "roofing quote") lists only businesses whose live doors take it. From rules version 12, one near a place with no match for every word is run again with its kind's words. How results are ordered, and when one is left out: https://surfingdog.ai/v1/ranking.

radius_km.description: Another name for near's radius_km, as GET /v1/businesses writes it: how far from near, or from a town query names, in kilometres. Give it once: near.radius_km or radius_km.

requestable.description: A live door that declared it answers this kind. This only leaves businesses out.

source.description: member (through its inbox), registered (by the business), found (by this network on the business's own website); any of them. This only leaves businesses out.

name: search_businesses

outputSchema.description: Every field is described in this tool's outputSchema at https://network.surfingdog.ai/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json.

title: Find businesses
